description: Wire vectors of the Produce API (key 0, v0 to v9), replayed by tests/Compliance.

vectors.description: Produce request v3 with RequiredAcks = 1, the null TransactionalId of a producer that is not in a transaction, and a record batch of the message format v2 with two records - the first of them with a key and two headers, the second without either. Version 3 is the only version that can carry any of the three.

Produce response v3 of a topic that keeps the CreateTime of the producer. The frame is the one of version 2, byte for byte - PRODUCE_RESPONSE_V3 is PRODUCE_RESPONSE_V2 in Protocol.java @ 0.11.0.3 - so it carries the base offset the batch was appended at, the LogAppendTime -1 of a CreateTime topic and the ThrottleTime of version 1, and no log_start_offset: that field is Kafka 1.0.

The answer of the same request for a topic created with message.timestamp.type=LogAppendTime: the broker overwrote the timestamps of the whole batch with its own clock and reports that value as the LogAppendTime of the partition.

Produce request v2 with RequiredAcks = 1 and a message set of two uncompressed messages of message format v1, the second one without a key. The body is byte for byte the one of v0 and v1, only the api version of the header differs.

Produce response v2 of a topic that keeps the CreateTime of the producer: the base offset the message set was appended at, the LogAppendTime that version 2 added behind it - -1, "the broker stamped nothing" - and the ThrottleTime of version 1, which closes the answer.

The answer of the same request for a topic created with message.timestamp.type=LogAppendTime: the broker overwrote the timestamp of every message of the batch with its own clock and reports that value as the LogAppendTime of the partition, 1788933842981 = 2026-09-09T06:04:02.981Z.
Produce request v1 with RequiredAcks = 1 and a message set of two uncompressed messages, the second one without a key. The body is the one of v0, only the api version of the header differs.
Produce response v1: the base offset the message set was appended at, followed by the ThrottleTime that version 1 added at the very end of the answer (0, the broker enforces no producer quota).

Produce response v1 of a client that exceeded its producer_byte_rate quota: the batch was appended, and the broker held the answer back for 793 ms and reported that delay as the ThrottleTime of the response.
Produce request v0 with RequiredAcks = 1 and a message set of two uncompressed messages, the second one without a key.
Produce response v0: the base offset the message set was appended at, and no ThrottleTime - that field only exists in v1.

Produce v3 of an idempotent producer: the record batch v2 carries the producer id the broker handed out, the epoch 0 and the base sequence 0 of the two records it holds, and `acks` is -1, which the guarantee of KIP-98 requires. The transactional id of the request stays null - the batch is idempotent, not transactional.

The answer to the very same batch sent a second time, the retry of a batch whose acknowledgement got lost: the broker recognises the triple (producer id, epoch, sequence range) of the batch it appended last and answers the error code 0 with the offset of that **original** append, without writing anything. The `LogAppendTime` of 1788959375324 gives it away: the topic keeps the CreateTime of the producer, so the first append answered -1 there, while a duplicate is answered with the timestamp the log holds for the batch.
Produce v3 whose record batch starts at the sequence 9 while the broker expects 2 for this producer id and partition, the gap that an idempotent producer must never leave.

The answer to a sequence with a gap in it: the error code 45 (OutOfOrderSequenceNumber) and no offset. The same code answers a duplicate of a batch that is not the last one the broker appended, because the duplicate check of a 0.11.0.3 broker only knows that last batch.

Produce v3 of a transactional producer: the request carries the transactional id `t8-vectors-txn` - a plain and an idempotent producer send `null` there - and bit 4 of the record batch attributes (0x10) marks the batch itself as transactional. The producer id, the epoch and the base sequence are the ones of the idempotent producer underneath.

Produce v4 of a record batch of two records into one partition. The body is the one of version 3, byte for byte; what the version states is that the client understands the error code 56 KAFKA_STORAGE_ERROR.
The answer of that request: the version 2 frame, without the LogStartOffset that version 5 appended to every partition entry.
Produce v5 of a record batch of two records into a partition whose first two records have been deleted by a DeleteRecords request. The body is the one of version 3.

The answer of that request. The LogStartOffset that version 5 appended to every partition entry reports the offset the log of the partition begins at - 2, because the DeleteRecords request removed everything below it - and it is what tells an idempotent producer that a 59 UNKNOWN_PRODUCER_ID is spurious.

The first of five batches of one idempotent producer, sent a second time after four more batches of the same producer id went into the partition - the retry a producer would send if the acknowledgements of five batches in a row had been lost. The frame is byte for byte the one that was appended, only the correlation id differs: the producer id 574, the epoch 0 and the base sequence 0 are the ones the original append carried.

The answer of a **1.1.1** broker to that duplicate: the error code 0 and the base offset 0 of the original append, four batches back. A 0.11.0.3 broker, which kept a single batch per producer and partition, answered 45 (OutOfOrderSequence) for anything but the very last one; `ProducerStateEntry.NumBatchesToRetain = 5` @ 1.0.2 and 1.1.1 is what widened it. The `LogAppendTime` of 1789060611437 gives the duplicate away - the topic keeps the CreateTime of the producer, so a real append answers -1 there - and the `LogStartOffset` of version 5 is 0, the partition being untouched.

The next batch of that producer - base sequence 5, the five records of the batches above being acknowledged - sent after a DeleteRecords request removed every record of the partition. The producer knows nothing of the deletion, so the frame is the ordinary next one of the sequence.

The error code **59** UNKNOWN_PRODUCER_ID (Kafka 1.0): `ProducerStateManager.truncateHead()` dropped the entry of every producer whose last record fell below the new log start offset, and a batch of a producer the broker has no entry for that does not start at the sequence 0 is answered with this code rather than with the 45 of a 0.11.0.3 broker. The `LogStartOffset` of 5 is the whole point of Produce v5: it is above the offset 4 this producer last had acknowledged, so the records really were deleted, and the client numbers the partition from 0 again instead of throwing its producer id away.

Produce request v6 with RequiredAcks = 1, the null TransactionalId of a producer that is not in a transaction and a record batch of the message format v2 with two records. The body is the body of version 3, byte for byte - ProduceRequest.json @ 2.8.2 has no field above version 3 - and what version 6 (Kafka 2.0, KIP-219) states is that the client waits out the throttle time of the answer itself.

Produce response v6 of an unthrottled append: the frame of version 5, byte for byte, with the base offset the batch was appended at, the LogAppendTime -1 of a CreateTime topic, the log start offset of version 5 and the ThrottleTime 0 of a client without a quota.

The answer of a Produce v6 request that a producer_byte_rate quota of 1024 bytes per second throttled: the batch was appended - the error code is 0 and the base offset is real - and the ThrottleTime behind the topics array is the 2381 ms the broker is about to mute the channel for. The answer itself arrived about 1 ms after the request was written: KIP-219 (Kafka 2.0) makes a broker answer a request of these versions first and delay afterwards, where a version 5 request would have waited the whole 2381 ms before its answer arrived.

Produce request v7 (Kafka 2.1, KIP-110) of one record batch: the frame of version 3, byte for byte - ProduceRequest.json @ 2.8.2 has no field above version 3 - with another number in its header. What version 7 states is that the record sets of the request may carry the compression type 4, zstd; a lower version that does is refused with the error code 76.

The answer v7: the frame of version 5, unchanged - ProduceResponse.json @ 2.8.2 has no field above version 5 - with the base offset, the log append time -1 of a CreateTime topic, the log start offset and the throttle time.

The answer of a 2.8.2 broker to a Produce v6 whose record set is compressed with zstd: the error code 76 UNSUPPORTED_COMPRESSION_TYPE for the partition, with the offset -1. ProduceRequest.validateRecords @ 2.8.2 refuses the codec below version 7 while it parses the request, and the broker answers the partition with the code instead of closing the connection.

Produce request v8 (Kafka 2.4, KIP-467) of one record batch: the frame of version 3, byte for byte - ProduceRequest.json @ 2.8.2 has no field above version 3 - with another number in its header. What version 8 states is that the client understands the record_errors and the error_message that a refused batch is answered with.

The answer v8 of an accepted batch: the frame of version 5 with two more fields per partition - an EMPTY record_errors array (00 00 00 00) and a null error_message (ff ff) behind the log start offset. Nothing was refused, so there is nothing to name.

Produce request v8 of a batch of three records, the second and the third of them WITHOUT a key, to a topic that is configured cleanup.policy=compact. A compacted log is keyed by definition, so the broker refuses the whole batch - and version 8 is the first version that can say which of the records it refused it for.

The answer: the error code 87 INVALID_RECORD for the partition, the offsets -1 of a batch that was never appended, and the record_errors array of KIP-467 - one entry per refused record, with its BATCH INDEX (the position inside the sent batch, counted from 0, not an offset) - followed by the error_message that summarizes the common cause. This is the whole point of version 8: every version below it answers the same 87 and nothing else.

1.batchIndexErrorMessage: Compacted topic cannot accept message without key in topic partition t2-24-compacted-0.

2.batchIndexErrorMessage: Compacted topic cannot accept message without key in topic partition t2-24-compacted-0.

partitions.errorMessage: One or more records have been rejected

vectors.description: The answer of a version 7 request to the very same refused batch: the error code 87 and the offsets -1, and not a byte more. A producer that speaks version 7 or below learns that its batch was refused and nothing about which record caused it - the gap KIP-467 closed.
